rows.evidence: Q1: Section IV (Results) and Section V (Evaluation), Table I - the authors implemented their trajectory equations in MATLAB and report their own model runs (time and position vectors, irrigation error, water used per segment and water savings of up to 122.9% per segment and 31.5% overall).
rows.notes: The study is a pure simulation: a trajectory-design algorithm is run in MATLAB on a CWSI image of a vineyard taken from another publication (Bellvert et al. 2014, Fig. 3). The reported water savings (Table I) are computed analytically by comparing the modelled volume applied against a modelled 'traditional' homogeneous volume; no UAV flight, no actual irrigation and no field measurement of water use or crop stress were made, and the model output is never checked against observations. The authors themselves state in the Conclusion that experimental tests to back up these results should be carried out. Under the rules a model never compared with measurements from the real system does not count as own evidence on the claim, so Q2 is 'no'. The 122.9% figure is also an artefact of the authors' definition (saving expressed relative to the volume used, not the traditional volume).

notes: Full text appears complete (conference paper, 2017 IEEE CCAC). The study is a simulation-only methodology paper; its water-saving figures are model outputs with no experimental validation.
